key_insight: Ligand-engineered AgBiS2 nanocrystal films enable stable near-infrared sub-cells for tandem photovoltaics, including a demonstrated 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandem.
engineering_relevance: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables one-step deposition of thicker absorber films while preserving efficient charge extraction, addressing a key constraint on near-infrared harvesting.
method: Model tandem performance using the measured AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Passivate AgBiS2 nanocrystals through solution-phase ligand exchange.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under continuous illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
